newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: SMITH AN "AMATEUR": AIR TRAFFIC CONTROLLERS
Millionaire aviator, Dick Smith has described as "absolute rubbish" complaints made against him by air traffic controllers.
This follows Mr Smith's attemps to join the Civil Aviation Safety Authority Board which is embroiled in a bitter feud with the Federal Government which wants the current Board sacked.
Air traffic controllers spokesman Peter McGuane says that while Mr Smith is an enthusiastic amateur, he doesn't have the appropriate background to be on the Board.
Mr McGuane's also accused Mr Smith of harrassing air traffic controllers, and of displaying poor airmanship.
The Senate is set to consider the Government's attempt to enlarge the Board effectively allowing it to reduce the power of existing directors this week.
REVIEW OF TOP-END'S PROSTITUTION REGULATION ACT
Sex workers in the Northern Territory will give their views today on how well the Prostitution Regulation Act is working.
The Attorney General's Department is conducting the first review of the act.
Brothels are illegal in the Territory, with sex workers being licensed and working for an escort agency, or unlicensed and working solo.
People with convictions related to drugs or violent acts are unable to get a licence.
Escort agency operators were consulted at a confidential meeting last week.
WHALE PUT DOWN AFTER RESCUE ATTEMPTS FAIL
In New South Wales, National Parks and Wildlife Service officials have put down a three-metre melon-headed whale which beached itself near Forster, north of Newcastel at the weekend.
The whale became stranded at Seven Mile Beach on Saturday night and was taken overland by truck to the Tuncurry rock pool where volunteers attempted to save the animal.
National Parks representative Brian Davies says the whale had shown signs of recovering, but its condition later deteriorated.
A post mortem examination will be carried out this week to try to determine why the mammal beached itself.
CYCLONE ITA FORMS IN CORAL SEA
In north Queensland, a tropical cyclone warning has been issued for coastal and island communities between Cardwell and Bowen with a cyclone watch extending south to Mackay.
Category One Cyclone Ita is centred about 370 kilometres east of Cairns and moving steadily southward.
The weak cyclone developed in the Coral Sea overnight and is expected to produce Gales between Cardwell and Bowen later today.
Ita's expected to turn southwest towards the coast during the morning.
JAPANESE TOURIST DIES CLIMBING ULURU
Another tourist has died while climbing Uluru in Central Australia.
The Japanese man died yesterday morning when he was about 200-metres up the rock.
Police have not confirmed the cause of death, but say he tumbled away from the chain he was holding onto and fellow tourists were unable to revive him.
FIRE HAS BADLY DAMAGED A CATHOLIC SCHOOL IN SYDNEY'S WEST.
A fire brigade spokesman says the blaze broke out in a two-storey building at the Holy Family Catholic School in Granville about 11 o'clock last night.
Several classrooms and their contents were severely damaged.
Meanwhile, on Sydney's northern beaches, a woman was slightly injured when her house caught alight.
The fire apparently started in the loungeroom of the two-story home in Fairlight.
The woman was treated at the scene for smoke inhalation.
VACCINE TO BE BROUGHT IN TO FIGHT ANTHRAX
Victoria's Natural Resources Department will bring in 50 thousand vaccine doses from overseas to continue the battle against anthrax in the Goulburn Valley.
During the weekend, anthrax was confirmed at four more properties, bringing the total to 79.
The department's regional manager, Clive Noble, is expecting more vaccine to be flown in from the United States or Europe this week.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
